data.change_summary:
The habitat registry and colonizable-area model is already fully implemented. No code changes were needed.

Existing implementation includes:
- HabitatKind enum with all 5 target habitats (FilterMedia, GlassHardscape, PlantSurfaces, SubstrateSurface, SubstrateDeep) in types/habitat.rs
- HabitatEntry struct with colonizable_area_cm2 and three bounded [0,1] exposure modifiers (flow, oxygen, light), all documented and serializable
- compute_habitat_registry() derives areas from geometry (wall_area_cm2, footprint_area_cm2, hardscape_area_cm2), hardware (filter.media_area_cm2), plant state (biomass_g × guild-specific SLA), and substrate layers (colonizable_area_cm2)
- Exposure modifiers are responsive to filter flow/clogging, aeration intensity, light intensity, plant crowding, substrate low-oxygen tendency, rooted plant root-zone O2 boost, and depth attenuation
- Registry stored as Vec<HabitatEntry> on TankState with #[serde(default)], recomputed daily in engine day-boundary pipeline
- Schema v5→v6 migration adds habitat_registry, geometry.hardscape_area_cm2, and filter.media_area_cm2 with post-migration fixup
- Public API exports: HabitatKind, HabitatEntry, compute_habitat_registry(), find_habitat()
- 24 comprehensive tests covering serialization round-trips, area computation, modifier sensitivity, bounds validation, plant biomass responsiveness, registry invariants, and geometry scaling
outstanding_risks: TankSnapshot (API serialization view) does not currently include habitat_registry data — downstream consumers that read snapshots rather than full TankState won't see habitat information until the snapshot type is extended

Periphyton capacity in algae_growth.rs uses a single colonizable area value rather than reading from the habitat registry — this will need wiring when tanksim-6e5.5.3 splits periphyton pools by habitat

Nitrification in nitrogen_cycle.rs is still global (not habitat-indexed) — the registry provides the modifiers but downstream systems (tanksim-6e5.5.2) must opt in to use them for habitat-specific biofilter capacity scaling

steps.description: Explore codebase to understand existing types, state, geometry, substrate, hardware, plant models, engine orchestration, save/migration, and test coverage

Verify types/habitat.rs contains HabitatKind enum with all 5 target habitats (FilterMedia, GlassHardscape, PlantSurfaces, SubstrateSurface, SubstrateDeep) and HabitatEntry struct with colonizable_area_cm2 and bounded [0,1] exposure modifiers

Verify compute_habitat_registry() derives colonizable areas from geometry, hardware config, plant biomass (via guild-specific SLA constants), and substrate layer properties rather than hardcoded constants

Verify flow, oxygen, and light exposure modifiers are documented, bounded via .clamp(0.0, 1.0), and responsive to relevant scenario inputs (filter flow/clogging, aeration intensity, light intensity, plant crowding, substrate low-oxygen tendency, rooted plant root-zone boost, depth attenuation)
Verify habitat_registry: Vec<HabitatEntry> is serialized on TankState with #[serde(default)] and recomputed daily in engine.rs day-boundary pipeline via compute_habitat_registry()
Verify save.rs schema v5→v6 migration handles habitat_registry, geometry.hardscape_area_cm2, and filter.media_area_cm2 addition with post-migration fixup for pre-existing saves
Verify public API exports (HabitatKind, HabitatEntry, compute_habitat_registry, find_habitat) via types/mod.rs and lib.rs pub use types::*

Run 24 habitat_registry tests: all pass covering serialization round-trips, area computation correctness, modifier sensitivity, bounds validation under extreme inputs, plant biomass responsiveness, registry invariants, and geometry scaling
Run full test suite (200+ tests) and clippy: all pass with zero warnings, confirming habitat registry integrates cleanly with existing systems

validation_evidence: 24/24 habitat_registry tests pass: habitat_kind_serialization_round_trip, habitat_entry_serialization_round_trip, full_registry_serialization_round_trip, filter_media_area_matches_hardware_config, filter_media_area_zero_when_disabled, glass_hardscape_area_equals_wall_plus_hardscape, plant_surfaces_area_from_biomass_and_sla, plant_surfaces_zero_without_plants, substrate_surface_area_equals_footprint, substrate_surface_zero_without_substrate, substrate_deep_area_sums_layer_colonizable_areas, higher_flow_increases_flow_exposure, aeration_boosts_oxygen_exposure, clogging_reduces_filter_oxygen, light_intensity_affects_exposure, rooted_plants_boost_substrate_surface_oxygen, plant_crowding_reduces_light_exposure, substrate_deep_always_dark, substrate_deep_oxygen_capped, all_modifiers_bounded_under_extreme_inputs, plant_biomass_change_updates_area, registry_covers_all_habitat_kinds, find_habitat_returns_none_for_missing, larger_tank_produces_larger_wall_and_substrate_areas
Full workspace test suite passes: 200+ tests across tank_core, tank_scenarios, tank_harness, tank_data, tank_tui, tank_api with 0 failures
cargo clippy clean: zero warnings across all crates in the workspace
Serialization verified: HabitatKind, HabitatEntry, and full Vec<HabitatEntry> registry all round-trip correctly through serde_json

Area computation verified: FilterMedia matches hardware.filter.media_area_cm2, GlassHardscape equals wall_area_cm2 + hardscape_area_cm2, PlantSurfaces equals sum(biomass_g * SLA) with FastStem=40 and RootRosette=25 cm²/g, SubstrateSurface equals footprint_area_cm2, SubstrateDeep sums layer.colonizable_area_cm2

Modifier bounds verified: all_modifiers_bounded_under_extreme_inputs test exercises 4 extreme scenarios (max_everything, min_everything, max_clogging_with_filter, huge_tank) and confirms all modifiers in [0,1] and areas >= 0
Plant biomass responsiveness verified: plant_biomass_change_updates_area test confirms PlantSurfaces area tracks biomass changes (5g→200cm², 20g→800cm² for FastStem)

Modifier sensitivity verified: tests confirm higher flow increases flow_exposure, aeration boosts oxygen_exposure, clogging reduces FilterMedia oxygen, light intensity increases light_exposure, rooted plants boost SubstrateSurface oxygen, crowding reduces GlassHardscape light, SubstrateDeep always dark (0.0 light) and oxygen-capped (<=0.2)
